statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58043 is a Node.js Permission Model over-grant: when --allow-fs-read or --allow-fs-write paths share a prefix, the radix tree that stores them marked the node created by splitting a shared prefix as a granted path, so with --permission a path that is only a prefix of the granted ones (for example /tmp/secret when /tmp/secret1, /tmp/secret2 and /tmp/secret3 are granted) became readable or writable. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.2, released 2026-07-29: the July 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases, lists 22.x among the affected release lines, and the 22.23.2 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.2, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/440329f624 ('permission: avoid granting radix split nodes'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-58043 and is in the v22.23.2 tag and not in v22.23.1; outside tests it changes src/permission/fs_permission.h. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58043, lists Node.js 22 releases up to 22.23.1 as affected. The DHI nodejs-22 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. Each published nodejs-22 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-22-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-22-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-27, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 22.23.2-r0, 22.23.3-r0, 22.23.4-r0, 22.23.4-r1, 22.23.4-r2 and 22.23.5-r0 report v22.23.2 through v22.23.5 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 22.22.0-r0, 22.22.1-r0, 22.22.2-r0, 22.22.2-r1, 22.22.3-r0, 22.23.0-r0 and 22.23.1-r0 report v22.22.0 through v22.23.1 and are affected. As a check, this fix is C++ code with no new string, so we ran upstream's regression case for it (test/parallel/test-permission-fs-read.js in the fix commit: grant secret1, secret2 and secret3 and check access to secret in the same directory) against the shipped node binary. On aarch64, in every published build, 22.22.0-r0 through 22.23.1-r0 report secret as granted and read it, while 22.23.2-r0 and every later build report it as not granted and refuse the read with ERR_ACCESS_DENIED; on x86_64 we ran it on 22.22.0-r0 and 22.23.1-r0, which read the file, and on 22.23.2-r0 and 22.23.5-r0, which refuse it. secret1 stays granted in every build tested. 22.23.2-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
